key_insight: Rectified-flow generation paired with exact latent-space refinement enables concurrent optimization of printable bone-scaffold microstructures and their spatial placement to meet mechanical targets.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports highly porous, mechanically constrained implants and could extend to topology–microstructure co-design for metal additive manufacturing.
method: Generate periodic lattice cells using a conditional rectified-flow model.
Refine cells in latent space using exact finite-element homogenization sensitivities.
Jointly optimize cell geometry and spatial assignment under mechanical and feature-size constraints.
evidence_signal: All eight rabbit-benchmark refinements achieved under 1% maximum relative error across six target moduli; human femur designs reached 63% cortical porosity with compliance within 2% and 84% cancellous porosity with strain-energy deviations below 0.25%.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational benchmarks; physical print fidelity, fatigue durability, and biological performance remain to be validated.
paper_title: Concurrent two-scale topology optimization of printable bone scaffolds via rectified-flow generation and exact latent-space refinement
